P10j: So this is not just a problem for me, it's a problem in every community, but especially in communities which form naturally over time as I'm describing may happen in my case. In such cases, there's no formal community and no formal rules until people decide to come together to make them. It doesn't make sense to do that at first, if I'm the only one there and I don't know who else will be there that I could trust. If there's one other person who comes to visit, it also doesn't make sense, so there's a critical mass point at which people decide "we were just living together like friends, but now we want to formalize the community". If I could find a group of people and join them right now, this problem wouldn't exist. I haven't found them yet.
P16q: The boundary is simple. These aren't principles to give the community power over me, they're principles I choose to guide my own practice. The six months of peer counseling before medicine is something else: a rule the community holds for its ceremonies.
